testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Using brakes creates heat. If too much heat builds up, what happens?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes are made to handle a lot of heat. But when brakes get too hot, they may fade and lose stopping power. Drivers should also use engine braking to help slow the vehicle.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Large trucks use air brakes. Air brake systems use compressed air to operate.

questions.question: What gets removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on in an air brake vehicle, what should the driver do?

options.text: Test the brakes while driving, but continue if they seem okay.

questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning comes on, you must stop and park safely as soon as possible. You need to keep enough braking power to stop safely.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil. These can harm the system if they build up. Drain valves help remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within how long?
questions.explanation: In single air systems, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in 3 minutes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system has a leak, what happens?

options.text: The other system may not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other system may not be affected.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake vehicle, what does the air pressure move?
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters. This twists the brake camshafts.

questions.question: At what air pressure does the compressor governor stop pumping air?
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops the compressor at 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: When the safety relief valve in an air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob to apply the parking brake. Push it back in to release it.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air?

options.text: This is normal and nothing to worry about.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the safety relief valve releases air, something is wrong with the brake system. Have a mechanic inspect and repair it.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: When can you rely on front wheel braking to work?
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works under all road conditions, including ice and snow. Front wheels are unlikely to skid.

questions.question: What should you do with the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Use it only when parked on a slope.
Do not use it, as it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parked. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if brakes are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: The ____ are turned on by an electric switch that the brake pedal activates.
questions.explanation: When you push the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems within 45 seconds.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving?

options.text: Exit the roadway safely as soon as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway safely as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving, safely exit the roadway and park. Low air pressure means your brakes will not stop the vehicle safely.

questions.question: Where are the braking mechanisms located in a brake drum?
questions.explanation: The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are located inside the brake drum.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. It helps drivers know if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle going 55 mph on a flat road needs about ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and actual braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under good conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: When parking on a flat surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only after applying the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parking on a flat surface. If your vehicle does not have spring brakes, this is necessary to prevent the trailer from moving.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
One air brake system with two different sets of controls.
One system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the rear brakes while the other controls the front brakes.
